**3. Membership**

3.1 Membership is open to any entity that operates an online marketplace in Australia, or that provides material trust and safety services to such marketplaces, and that is willing to commit to the Committee's Principles of Engagement (Schedule A).

3.2 Founding members as at the adoption of this Charter are listed in Schedule B. Additional members may be admitted by a simple majority vote of the existing members.

3.3 Each member shall appoint one primary representative and may appoint one alternate. Representatives should hold a role with sufficient authority to commit their organisation to agreed actions.

3.4 A member may withdraw from the Committee at any time by written notice to the Secretariat. Withdrawal does not affect obligations incurred prior to the notice taking effect.

**4. Officers and Secretariat**

4.1 The Committee shall have a Chair and a Deputy Chair, elected by members for a two-year term. The Chair presides over meetings and represents the Committee externally.

4.2 The Secretariat is provided by a member organisation or an external service provider, as determined by the Committee. The Secretariat maintains records, circulates documents, and supports the Chair.

4.3 The Chair may establish working groups for specific issues. Working groups report to the Committee and operate under terms of reference approved by the Committee.

**5. Meetings**

5.1 The Committee shall meet at least four times per calendar year, with a target of one meeting per quarter. Additional meetings may be called by the Chair or at the request of at least one-third of members.

5.2 Meetings may be held in person, by video conference, or in a hybrid format. A quorum shall be a majority of member representatives entitled to vote.

5.3 Members are expected to attend all meetings. A member who misses three consecutive meetings without a reasonable explanation may be asked by the Chair to confirm their ongoing commitment.

5.4 The Secretariat shall circulate an agenda at least five business days before each meeting. Minutes shall be drafted within ten business days after the meeting and circulated for approval at the next meeting.

5.5 Decisions shall be made by consensus where possible. If a vote is required, each member has one vote. Unless otherwise stated in this Charter, decisions require a simple majority of those present and voting.

**7. FUNCTIONS OF THE COMMITTEE**

7.1 The Committee has the functions conferred on it by the Act, the Commission, and this Charter. In performing its functions, the Committee shall have regard to the objects of the Act, including the promotion of safe, trusted, and transparent online marketplaces for Australian consumers and businesses.

7.2 Without limiting clause 7.1, the functions of the Committee are:

(a) to advise the Commission on matters relating to the safety and integrity of online marketplaces, including the identification of emerging risks and harms to Australian consumers;

(b) to review, and advise the Commission on, the effectiveness of the Marketplace Integrity Standards (the **Standards**) made under the Act, including recommending amendments to the Standards where the Committee considers it necessary or desirable;

(c) to consider, and provide advice to the Commission on, applications for the approval of industry codes of practice submitted under Part 5 of the Act, and on any subsequent amendments to approved codes;

(d) to monitor the implementation by marketplaces of the Standards and approved codes, and to report to the Commission on the compliance of marketplaces with their obligations under the Act;

(e) to establish and oversee technical advisory groups, working groups, or other sub-committees as the Committee considers appropriate to address specific safety or integrity issues;

(f) to provide advice to the Commission on the exercise of its information-gathering and investigation powers under the Act, including the use of market surveillance and data analytics;

(g) to facilitate information sharing and cooperation between marketplaces, consumer and business advocacy groups, law enforcement agencies, and other relevant bodies in relation to marketplace safety and integrity matters;

(h) to provide advice on research priorities and the commissioning of research into matters relevant to the safety and integrity of online marketplaces; and

(i) to undertake such other functions as are conferred on the Committee by the Act, the Commission, or this Charter.

7.3 The functions in clause 7.2 are advisory and facilitative in nature. Nothing in this Charter, and no advice or report of the Committee, shall be construed as authorising the Committee to make, amend, or revoke the Standards, to approve or reject a code of practice, to make a determination under the Act, or to exercise any power or discretion vested in the Commissioner or the Commission under the Act.

7.4 In performing its functions, the Committee shall have regard to the principles of:

(a) **proportionality** – that any advice or recommendation should be proportionate to the risk of harm identified and the burden it may impose on marketplaces, particularly small and medium enterprises;

(b) **evidence-based decision-making** – that advice and recommendations should be informed by the best available evidence, including data, research, and consultation with affected stakeholders;

(c) **transparency** – that the Committee’s processes and advice should be open and accountable, subject to any confidentiality obligations under the Act or this Charter; and

(d) **cooperation** – that the Committee should seek to work constructively with marketplaces, regulators, and other stakeholders to achieve the objects of the Act.

7.5 The Committee may, at its discretion, publish guidance, discussion papers, or other documents to assist marketplaces and the public in understanding the Committee’s advice or the operation of the Standards, provided that such publication is consistent with the Committee’s functions and any confidentiality requirements under the Act.

**8. Subcommittees and Working Groups**

8.1 The Committee may, by resolution, establish one or more subcommittees or working groups to assist it in performing its functions. 8.2 A subcommittee or working group may be established to address a particular matter or class of matters within the Committee’s functions, including but not limited to:

(a) emerging technology risks, such as the use of generative artificial intelligence in listing content, review generation, or seller communications;

(b) specific categories of harm, including counterfeit and unsafe physical goods, financial scams, and the online sale of age-restricted products;

(c) data sharing and research coordination between marketplaces, regulators, and consumer or business advocacy groups;

(d) the development of educational materials or guidance for small and medium enterprises on compliance with the Standards; and

(e) the monitoring of international regulatory developments relevant to marketplace safety and integrity.

8.3 The Committee shall determine the terms of reference for each subcommittee or working group at the time of its establishment. The terms of reference shall specify:

(a) the purpose and scope of the body’s work;

(b) the functions delegated to it and any limits on those functions;

(c) the period for which the body is established;

(d) the reporting requirements to the Committee; and

(e) any arrangements for the co-option of external expertise.

8.4 Unless the Committee resolves otherwise, a subcommittee or working group shall be chaired by a member of the Committee. 8.5 A subcommittee or working group shall not make any public statement or publication on behalf of the Committee, and shall not correspond with marketplaces, the Commission, or other external parties in the name of the Committee, without the prior written approval of the Committee.

9.3 A delegation under this clause does not prevent the Committee from exercising the delegated power or function itself. The Committee may revoke or vary a delegation at any time by resolution.

9.4 Unless the Committee resolves otherwise, a delegation to a subcommittee or working group is confined to the formulation of advice or recommendations to the Committee, and does not include a power to make decisions on behalf of the Committee or to commit the Committee to a particular position.

The Chair may, however, permit a proposed amendment to be considered without such notice where the Chair is satisfied that the amendment is of a minor or machinery nature and that no member will be prejudiced by the shorter notice.

15.5 A resolution to amend this Charter shall not be passed unless it is supported by at least two-thirds of the members present and voting. A member who abstains shall not be counted for the purpose of this clause.

The following is a simplified outline of this Act:

This Act requires operators of online marketplaces to take reasonable steps to prevent the supply of unsafe goods and the provision of unsafe services through their marketplaces.

Part 2 sets out the core obligations of marketplace operators, including duties to conduct safety risk assessments, to implement safety response procedures, and to cooperate with the national regulator.

Part 3 deals with the national regulator’s information-gathering and investigation powers.

Part 4 establishes a framework for the making of safety standards and bans.

Part 5 provides for enforcement, including infringement notices and civil penalties.

**Part 3 — Obligations of marketplace operators**

**20 Obligations of marketplace operators**

(1) A marketplace operator must, in relation to the online marketplace operated by the operator:

(a) take reasonable steps to ensure that goods and services supplied through the marketplace comply with any applicable safety standards; and

(b) take reasonable steps to ensure that goods and services supplied through the marketplace are safe; and

(c) establish and maintain a process for receiving and responding to notices of harm or potential harm relating to goods or services supplied through the marketplace; and

(d) comply with any requirements set out in a safety notice that applies to the operator; and

(e) cooperate with the national regulator in the performance of its functions under this Act.

(2) The obligations in subsection (1) apply only to the extent that the marketplace operator has control, whether directly or indirectly, over the supply of the goods or services concerned.

(3) For the purposes of subsection (2), a marketplace operator is taken to have control over the supply of goods or services if the operator:

(a) sets the terms and conditions under which the goods or services are supplied; or

(b) determines the price at which the goods or services are supplied; or

(c) manages the fulfilment, delivery, or collection of payment for the goods or services; or

(d) otherwise exercises a significant degree of influence over the supply.

(4) A marketplace operator is not required to take steps under subsection (1) in relation to goods or services if the operator has no reasonable means of identifying the supplier of the goods or services and has taken reasonable steps to do so.

**21 Safety duties of marketplace operators**

(1) A marketplace operator must not supply, or permit the supply of, goods or services through the online marketplace that the operator knows, or ought reasonably to know, are unsafe.

(2) Without limiting subsection (1), a marketplace operator ought reasonably to know that goods or services are unsafe if:

(a) the operator has received a notice from the national regulator, a government body, or a recognised safety authority that the goods or services are unsafe; or

(b) the operator has received a complaint or report from a consumer that the goods or services caused, or were involved in, an incident of harm; or

(c) the operator has received a report from a supplier that the goods or services are unsafe; or

(d) the goods or services have been the subject of a recall in Australia or in a foreign jurisdiction in the preceding 5 years and the operator has or ought to have access to information about that recall; or

(e) the operator has other information that would lead a reasonable person to conclude that the goods or services are unsafe.

(a) remove the goods or services from the marketplace; and

(b) take reasonable steps to notify any consumer who has purchased the goods or services within the preceding 12 months; and

(c) notify the national regulator in accordance with section 23.

**22 Directions by the national regulator**

(1) If the national regulator is satisfied that a marketplace operator is contravening, or has contravened, a provision of this Act, the national regulator may issue a written direction to the operator requiring the operator to do either or both of the following:

(a) take specified action to remedy the contravention or to prevent its recurrence;

(b) cease specified conduct that constitutes, or is likely to constitute, a contravention of this Act.

(2) A direction under subsection (1) must:

(a) be given to the marketplace operator by notice in writing; and

(b) specify the provision that the national regulator is satisfied is being or has been contravened; and

(c) specify the action required or the conduct to be ceased, as the case requires; and

(d) specify a reasonable period within which the operator must comply with the direction.

(3) The national regulator may vary or revoke a direction under this section by giving written notice to the marketplace operator.

(4) A direction under this section is not a legislative instrument.

(5) A marketplace operator who is given a direction under this section must comply with the direction within the period specified in the direction, or within such extended period as the national regulator allows.

**23 Notification of serious incidents and unsafe goods**

(1) A marketplace operator must notify the national regulator, in accordance with this section, of:

(a) any incident of serious harm arising out of the use of, or reasonably foreseeable misuse of, goods or services supplied through the online marketplace; and

(b) any goods or services supplied through the online marketplace that the operator has removed or restricted from the marketplace because the operator considers the goods or services to be unsafe.

(2) A notification under subsection (1) must be given:

**3. Membership**

3.1 Membership is open to any entity that operates an online marketplace in Australia, or that provides material trust and safety services to such marketplaces, and that is willing to commit to the Committee's Principles of Engagement (Schedule A).

3.2 Founding members as at the adoption of this Charter are listed in Schedule B. Additional members may be admitted by a simple majority vote of the existing members.

3.3 Each member shall appoint one primary representative and may appoint one alternate. Representatives should hold a role with sufficient authority to commit their organisation to agreed actions.

3.4 A member may withdraw from the Committee at any time by written notice to the Secretariat. Withdrawal does not affect obligations incurred prior to the notice taking effect.

**4. Officers and Secretariat**

4.1 The Committee shall have a Chair and a Deputy Chair, elected by members for a two-year term. The Chair presides over meetings and represents the Committee externally.

4.2 The Secretariat is provided by a member organisation or an external service provider, as determined by the Committee. The Secretariat maintains records, circulates documents, and supports the Chair.

4.3 The Chair may establish working groups for specific issues. Working groups report to the Committee and operate under terms of reference approved by the Committee.

**5. Meetings**

5.1 The Committee shall meet at least four times per calendar year, with a target of one meeting per quarter. Additional meetings may be called by the Chair or at the request of at least one-third of members.

5.2 Meetings may be held in person, by video conference, or in a hybrid format. A quorum shall be a majority of member representatives entitled to vote.

5.3 Members are expected to attend all meetings. A member who misses three consecutive meetings without a reasonable explanation may be asked by the Chair to confirm their ongoing commitment.

5.4 The Secretariat shall circulate an agenda at least five business days before each meeting. Minutes shall be drafted within ten business days after the meeting and circulated for approval at the next meeting.

5.5 Decisions shall be made by consensus where possible. If a vote is required, each member has one vote. Unless otherwise stated in this Charter, decisions require a simple majority of those present and voting.

**6. Powers and Limitations**

6.1 The Committee may:

(a) request information from members on a voluntary basis;

(b) commission research or surveys, subject to budget availability;

(c) issue public statements, guidance, or reports in the name of the Committee;

(d) invite non-members to present at meetings; and

(e) engage with regulators and government agencies.

6.2 The Committee has no power to:

(a) impose fines or sanctions on members or non-members;

(b) compel the disclosure of commercially sensitive information;

(c) make binding rules for the operation of any marketplace; or

6.3 Nothing in this Charter creates a legal partnership, agency, or joint venture among members. Each member remains responsible for its own compliance with applicable laws.

**7. Confidentiality and Information Handling**

7.1 Members and the Secretariat shall treat non-public information shared in Committee meetings as confidential, unless the information is already in the public domain or the disclosing party has authorised disclosure.

**8. Subcommittees and Working Groups**

8.1 The Committee may, by resolution, establish one or more subcommittees or working groups to assist it in performing its functions. Each such body shall be established for a specified purpose and, unless extended by further resolution, shall lapse twelve months after the date of its establishment.

8.2 A subcommittee or working group may be established to address a particular matter or class of matters within the Committee’s functions, including but not limited to:

(a) emerging technology risks, such as the use of generative artificial intelligence in listing content, review generation, or seller communications;

(b) specific categories of harm, including counterfeit and unsafe physical goods, financial scams, and the online sale of age-restricted products;

(c) data sharing and research coordination between marketplaces, regulators, and consumer or business advocacy groups;

(d) the development of educational materials or guidance for small and medium enterprises on compliance with the Standards; and

(e) the monitoring of international regulatory developments relevant to marketplace safety and integrity.

8.3 The Committee shall determine the terms of reference for each subcommittee or working group at the time of its establishment. The terms of reference shall specify:

(a) the purpose and scope of the body’s work;

(b) the functions delegated to it and any limits on those functions;

(c) the period for which the body is established;

(d) the reporting requirements to the Committee; and

(e) any arrangements for the co-option of external expertise.

8.4 Unless the Committee resolves otherwise, a subcommittee or working group shall be chaired by a member of the Committee. The chair of a subcommittee or working group shall provide a written report to the Committee at each regular meeting of the Committee following any meeting of the subcommittee or working group.

8.5 A subcommittee or working group shall not make any public statement or publication on behalf of the Committee, and shall not correspond with marketplaces, the Commission, or other external parties in the name of the Committee, without the prior written approval of the Committee.

8.6 A subcommittee or working group may invite, with the approval of the Committee, persons with relevant expertise to attend its meetings in an advisory capacity. Such persons shall be subject to the confidentiality obligations in clause 5 of this Charter and shall not be entitled to vote.

**9. Delegation of Powers**

9.1 The Committee may delegate to the Chair, the Deputy Chair, or to a subcommittee or working group established under clause 8, any of its powers or functions under this Charter, except this power of delegation.

9.2 A delegation under clause 9.1 shall be made by resolution and shall be recorded in the minutes of the meeting at which it is made. The delegation shall specify any conditions or limitations on the exercise of the delegated power or function.

9.3 A delegation under this clause does not prevent the Committee from exercising the delegated power or function itself. The Committee may revoke or vary a delegation at any time by resolution.

9.4 Unless the Committee resolves otherwise, a delegation to a subcommittee or working group is confined to the formulation of advice or recommendations to the Committee, and does not include a power to make decisions on behalf of the Committee or to commit the Committee to a particular position.

**11.2** The Committee shall not publish, and shall take reasonable steps to ensure that its members and advisers do not publish, any draft of a document referred to in clause 11.1, any working paper, or any other material prepared for the purpose of the Committee’s deliberations, unless the Committee has determined that publication would be in the public interest.

11.3 The Committee shall, in publishing any document under this Charter, have regard to the Commission’s guidelines on accessible communication (as amended from time to time).

11.4 Nothing in this clause prevents a member from making public statements about the work of the Committee in their personal capacity, provided that the member:

(a) does not purport to speak on behalf of the Committee or the Commission;

(b) does not disclose confidential information (including information relating to the deliberations of the Committee); and

(c) makes clear that the views expressed are the member’s own.

**12. Conflict of Interest**

12.1 A member shall, at the commencement of each regular meeting, and otherwise as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the matter, disclose to the Chair any actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest in relation to a matter before the Committee.

12.2 A conflict of interest includes, but is not limited to, any matter in which:

(a) the member, or a close associate of the member, has a financial interest;

(b) the member, or a close associate of the member, is a director, officer, employee, consultant, or contractor of a marketplace, or of a body representing marketplaces;

(c) the member has a professional or personal relationship with a person who is the subject of, or who has made a submission in relation to, a matter before the Committee; or

(d) the member has taken a public position on the matter that may, in the opinion of the Chair, give rise to a reasonable perception of bias.

12.3 Upon receiving a disclosure under clause 12.1, the Chair shall determine, having regard to the nature and extent of the conflict, whether the member may:

(a) participate in the Committee’s consideration of the matter;

(b) participate in the consideration but refrain from voting on the matter; or

(c) be excluded from the consideration of the matter, including from any part of the meeting at which the matter is discussed.

12.4 Where the Chair has a conflict of interest, the Deputy Chair shall perform the functions of the Chair under this clause in relation to that matter.

12.5 A member who is excluded from a matter under clause 12.3(c) shall not be present during the discussion or decision on the matter, and shall not receive any document or other material relating to the matter that is distributed to other members.

12.6 The Committee shall keep a register of disclosures of conflicts of interest, recording the nature of the conflict, the determination made by the Chair, and the date of the determination. The register shall be maintained for the life of the Committee and for a period of seven years after the Committee ceases to exist.

(a) modest hospitality of a routine kind; or

(b) a gift of nominal value that is disclosed to the Chair at the next meeting.

**14. Public Access to Committee Records**

14.1 Subject to clause 14.2, the following records of the Committee shall be made available on the Commission’s website within a reasonable time after their creation:

(a) the agenda for each meeting, excluding any part that relates to a matter the Chair has determined to be confidential under clause 13.2;

(b) the minutes of each meeting, once confirmed under clause 9.7, excluding any part that relates to a confidential matter;

(c) any determination or recommendation made by the Committee under this Charter, together with a short statement of reasons;

(d) the register of disclosures of conflicts of interest kept under clause 12.6, with the names of members redacted; and

(e) this Charter and any amendment to it.

14.2 The Committee may, by resolution, decide that a record or part of a record is not to be published where publication would:

(a) disclose personal information of a kind that would, in the opinion of the Committee, be unreasonable to publish;

(b) prejudice the investigation of a complaint or a matter referred to the Committee;

(c) disclose information that a marketplace has identified as confidential and that the Committee accepts is confidential; or

(d) otherwise be contrary to the public interest.

14.3 A decision under clause 14.2 shall be recorded in the minutes, together with the reason for the decision. The Committee shall review any such decision at least once every twelve months.

14.4 Nothing in this clause requires the Committee to publish a record that is the subject of a legal professional privilege claim.

**15. Amendment of this Charter**

15.1 The Committee may amend this Charter, in whole or in part, by resolution passed at a meeting of the Committee.

15.2 A proposal to amend this Charter may be made by:

(a) the Chair;

(b) any three members of the Committee acting jointly;

(c) the Commission; or

(d) the Minister.

15.3 Notice of a proposed amendment shall be given to all members of the Committee, the Commission, and the Minister, not less than twenty-one days before the meeting at which the proposal is to be considered. The notice shall set out the text of the proposed amendment and a short explanation of its purpose and effect.

15.4 The Committee shall not consider a proposed amendment unless the notice required by clause 15.3 has been given. The Chair may, however, permit a proposed amendment to be considered without such notice where the Chair is satisfied that the amendment is of a minor or machinery nature and that no member will be prejudiced by the shorter notice.

15.5 A resolution to amend this Charter shall not be passed unless it is supported by at least two-thirds of the members present and voting. A member who abstains shall not be counted for the purpose of this clause.

15.6 An amendment takes effect on the date specified in the resolution, which shall not be earlier than the date of the resolution. Where no date is specified, the amendment takes effect on the date of the resolution.

15.7 Each amendment shall be recorded in a schedule to this Charter, known as the Schedule of Amendments, which shall set out:

(a) the clause or clauses amended;

(b) the date of the resolution;

(c) the effective date of the amendment; and

(d) a brief description of the change.

15.8 The Schedule of Amendments shall be maintained by the Secretariat and shall be published with this Charter under clause 14.1(e).

**16. Interpretation and Glossary**

16.1 In this Charter, unless the contrary intention appears, words and expressions have the meanings given to them in the Act, and the following definitions apply.

16.2 The following terms are used throughout this Charter and in the Committee's published materials:

- **Act** means the *Online Marketplaces (Trust and Safety) Act 2021* (Cth), as amended from time to time.
- **Buyer** means a person who acquires, or proposes to acquire, goods or services through a marketplace, whether or not payment is made through the marketplace's own payment system.
- **Commission** means the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, or any successor body with responsibility for administering the Act.
- **Committee** means the Online Marketplaces Australia Trust & Safety Committee established by this Charter.
- **Marketplace** means an online platform, website, or application that facilitates transactions between sellers and buyers, whether the platform itself takes title to the goods or services or acts only as an intermediary. For the avoidance of doubt, this includes platforms that facilitate the sale of services, not only goods.
- **Member** means a person appointed to the Committee under clause 5, and includes the Chair and Deputy Chair.
- **Minister** means the Commonwealth Minister administering the Act.
- **Secretariat** means the office or unit within the Commission that provides administrative and research support to the Committee.
- **Seller** means a person who offers, or proposes to offer, goods or services for sale through a marketplace, whether in the course of business or otherwise.
- **Trust and safety incident** means an event or pattern of conduct on a marketplace that causes, or is reasonably likely to cause, significant harm to buyers, sellers, or the public, including but not limited to fraudulent listings, counterfeit goods, unsafe product recalls, identity theft, or the dissemination of materially misleading product information.

3 Simplified outline

The following is a simplified outline of this Act:

This Act requires operators of online marketplaces to take reasonable steps to prevent the supply of unsafe goods and the provision of unsafe services through their marketplaces.

Part 2 sets out the core obligations of marketplace operators, including duties to conduct safety risk assessments, to implement safety response procedures, and to cooperate with the national regulator.

Part 3 deals with the national regulator’s information-gathering and investigation powers.

Part 4 establishes a framework for the making of safety standards and bans.

Part 5 provides for enforcement, including infringement notices and civil penalties.

Part 6 contains miscellaneous matters, including administrative review and delegation.

4 Definitions

In this Act:

accredited third party has the meaning given by section 5.

associated payment service means a payment service that facilitates payment for a supply of goods or services through an online marketplace.

ban has the meaning given by section 33.

business day means a day that is not a Saturday, a Sunday, or a public holiday in the Australian Capital Territory.

civil penalty provision has the meaning given by section 41.

commencement day means the day on which sections 11 to 47 commence.

consumer has the meaning given by section 5.

country of origin, in relation to goods, has the meaning given by section 6.

**Part 3 — Obligations of marketplace operators**

**20 Obligations of marketplace operators**

(1) A marketplace operator must, in relation to the online marketplace operated by the operator:

(a) take reasonable steps to ensure that goods and services supplied through the marketplace comply with any applicable safety standards; and

(b) take reasonable steps to ensure that goods and services supplied through the marketplace are safe; and

(c) establish and maintain a process for receiving and responding to notices of harm or potential harm relating to goods or services supplied through the marketplace; and

(d) comply with any requirements set out in a safety notice that applies to the operator; and

(e) cooperate with the national regulator in the performance of its functions under this Act.

(2) The obligations in subsection (1) apply only to the extent that the marketplace operator has control, whether directly or indirectly, over the supply of the goods or services concerned.

(3) For the purposes of subsection (2), a marketplace operator is taken to have control over the supply of goods or services if the operator:

(a) sets the terms and conditions under which the goods or services are supplied; or

(b) determines the price at which the goods or services are supplied; or

(c) manages the fulfilment, delivery, or collection of payment for the goods or services; or

(d) otherwise exercises a significant degree of influence over the supply.

(4) A marketplace operator is not required to take steps under subsection (1) in relation to goods or services if the operator has no reasonable means of identifying the supplier of the goods or services and has taken reasonable steps to do so.

**21 Safety duties of marketplace operators**

(1) A marketplace operator must not supply, or permit the supply of, goods or services through the online marketplace that the operator knows, or ought reasonably to know, are unsafe.

(2) Without limiting subsection (1), a marketplace operator ought reasonably to know that goods or services are unsafe if:

(a) the operator has received a notice from the national regulator, a government body, or a recognised safety authority that the goods or services are unsafe; or

(b) the operator has received a complaint or report from a consumer that the goods or services caused, or were involved in, an incident of harm; or

(c) the operator has received a report from a supplier that the goods or services are unsafe; or

(d) the goods or services have been the subject of a recall in Australia or in a foreign jurisdiction in the preceding 5 years and the operator has or ought to have access to information about that recall; or

(e) the operator has other information that would lead a reasonable person to conclude that the goods or services are unsafe.

(c) notify the national regulator in accordance with section 23.

**Part 4 – Enforcement and Penalties**

**22 Directions by the national regulator**

(1) If the national regulator is satisfied that a marketplace operator is contravening, or has contravened, a provision of this Act, the national regulator may issue a written direction to the operator requiring the operator to do either or both of the following:

(a) take specified action to remedy the contravention or to prevent its recurrence;

(b) cease specified conduct that constitutes, or is likely to constitute, a contravention of this Act.

(2) A direction under subsection (1) must:

(a) be given to the marketplace operator by notice in writing; and

(b) specify the provision that the national regulator is satisfied is being or has been contravened; and

(c) specify the action required or the conduct to be ceased, as the case requires; and

(d) specify a reasonable period within which the operator must comply with the direction.

(3) The national regulator may vary or revoke a direction under this section by giving written notice to the marketplace operator.

(4) A direction under this section is not a legislative instrument.

(5) A marketplace operator who is given a direction under this section must comply with the direction within the period specified in the direction, or within such extended period as the national regulator allows.

**23 Notification of serious incidents and unsafe goods**

(1) A marketplace operator must notify the national regulator, in accordance with this section, of:

(a) any incident of serious harm arising out of the use of, or reasonably foreseeable misuse of, goods or services supplied through the online marketplace; and

(b) any goods or services supplied through the online marketplace that the operator has removed or restricted from the marketplace because the operator considers the goods or services to be unsafe.

(2) A notification under subsection (1) must be given:

(a) in the case of an incident of serious harm—within 48 hours after the operator becomes aware of the incident; and

(b) in the case of goods or services removed or restricted because they are considered unsafe—within 72 hours after the removal or restriction.

(3) A notification under subsection (1) must include:

(a) a description of the goods or services concerned; and

(b) the date and place of the incident or removal, if known; and

(c) the nature of the harm or the reason the goods or services are considered unsafe; and

(d) any other information prescribed by the regulations.

(4) The national regulator may, by written notice given to a marketplace operator, require the operator to provide further information in relation to a notification given under subsection (1) within a reasonable period specified in the notice.
